### What this finalization pass did
Starting from a partially-complete state, I closed the remaining gaps and verified every committed claim against source/evidence:

1. **Preserved all four issue-linked logs** (the issue body links *four* gists, not two): added `session-442ce104` + `session-5ddd6525` as gz + excerpt, and force-added the two pre-existing excerpts that were silently `.gitignore`d (`*.log`) — fixing broken README references. `source/` now tracks 10 files (2 JSON + 4 `.log.gz` + 4 excerpts), satisfying req #4/#5 "no data destroyed".

3. **Strengthened the root-cause evidence**: verified directly from the log banners/footers that **all four** sessions were OOM-killed (`Exit Code: 137`) inside a **40 ms** window (`19:10:49.782 → .822`) — a single host-OOM-cascade fingerprint, not two independent crashes. Updated the timeline, PR body, and case study to match.
4. **Sharpened the req-#8 audit table** with exact, source-verified call sites: `getIsolationSessionState` is the single reconciliation chokepoint inherited by its four callers (`monitorSessions`, `getRunningSessionItems`, `hasActiveSessionForUrlAsync`, `getRunningTrackedIsolationSessions`); corrected the `collectProcessDebugSessions` row (branches only on `status.exists`); confirmed the cleanup path's active→`{action:'keep', reason:'active-task'}` safety mapping in `cleanup.lib.mjs:257`.

Addressed in 0889fdce + 01b69783.

**1. Is the `$` session data deduplicated across `/queue`, `/limits`, cleanup (and the monitor)?**

Yes — verified. All `$ --status` reads funnel through the single `querySessionStatus()` chokepoint in `isolation-runner.lib.mjs`, and all `$ --list` reads through `listIsolationSessions()`. `/queue` and `/limits` count executing work via the session monitor (`getActiveSessionCount` → `getIsolationSessionState`), which itself calls `querySessionStatus`, so there is **one** reader of the raw `$` data, not several.

The one genuine duplicate was inside cleanup: `getActiveTasks()` re-derived live sessions from `screen -ls`/`tmux ls` (`listLiveSessionIds`) and then issued one `$ --status` per session (`listActiveTaskRefsFromSessions`). That path is now replaced by a single `listSessionTasks()` call reading the whole catalog from one `$ --list` — the same source the monitor/`/queue`/`/limits` already use. The two old helpers are kept but marked `@deprecated`.

**2. cleanup must show which PR and which session each hive-mind folder belongs to — including non-active folders.**

Done. Because `$ --list` reports finished sessions too (unlike the screen/tmux liveness scan), `listSessionTasks()` carries each session's `sessionId`, `status`, `workspace` and a `terminal` flag. The listing now renders, for **every** folder:

- active folder → `task <owner/repo PR #N, branch …, session …, status …, workspace …>`
- finished folder → `was <owner/repo PR #N, branch …, session …, status …>`
- neither matched → `issue #N` derived from the folder's branch

So you can always see, for active *and* non-active tasks, which PR/issue and which session a folder belongs (or belonged) to.

Note on matching: `$ --list` reports a session's `workingDirectory` as the launcher cwd (`/home/box`), not the per-task `gh-issue-solver-*` clone, so folder→session is matched via the GitHub URL in the command line → branch → folder branch (reusing the existing `buildActiveMatchers`/`folderMatchesActiveTask`).

Tests: added 3 unit tests in `tests/test-cleanup-1848.mjs` (non-active session annotation + issue-from-branch derivation); full cleanup suite 33/33 and the `#1927` suites green. Full write-up under `docs/case-studies/issue-1927/README.md` → "Review follow-up".

## Resume across surviving levels — addressed

Conflicts are resolved (the branch now merges `main` cleanly; PR went `CONFLICTING → MERGEABLE` after the push) and I worked through each point.

### Which level resumes — the survival hierarchy

Each level resumes at the level **above** the one that died. The first two already existed; this issue exposed a gap at the **top**:

| Level | Survives a kill of… | Resume mechanism | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AI tool (`claude`/`codex`/`gemini`) | one tool turn (usage limit, uncommitted-changes restart) | `/solve` re-invokes the tool with `--resume <sessionId>` (auto-continue / `solve.watch`) | already existed |
| `/solve` (detached screen/tmux/docker) | the AI tool process | `solve.mjs … --resume <id>` (`solve.resume-command.lib.mjs`) | already existed |
| `/hive` & Telegram bot | the **entire** detached `/solve` job (OOM/SIGKILL — this issue) | the bot's killed-session notification now carries a ready-to-run `solve <url> … --resume <lastSessionId>` | **new here** |

So **if `/solve` itself survives, it keeps using `--resume` on the tool directly — unchanged.** The new code only fills the case where the whole `/solve` job is killed and the surviving parent previously had no handle to resume.

### "Use the LAST of multiple sessions"

A single `/solve` run prints many `Session ID:` markers (auto-continue across limit resets, `watch` restarts, manual `--resume` chains). The new pure module [`src/session-resume.lib.mjs`](../blob/issue-1927-ae9e469b0606/src/session-resume.lib.mjs) reads the **last** marker from the captured log tail (`selectLastSessionId` / `readLastSessionIdFromLog`), with a filesystem fallback that picks the most-recent `<sessionId>.log` (`findLatestSessionLogId`). The end-to-end test proves the resume command names the **last** id, never the first.

### "Will not crash the system / backward compatibility preserved"

- The bot **surfaces** the resume command instead of auto-relaunching — a job that reliably OOMs would otherwise storm (worse than the silent hang this issue fixes). `planKilledSessionResume()` exists for any caller that *does* want automatic resume and caps it (default `maxAttempts: 1`).
- The resume section is **additive** via the existing `extraSections` mechanism, emitted **only** for `killed` `/solve` sessions (a successful session, or a `/hive` session, gets nothing), and the whole block is wrapped so a planning error can never break the completion notification.
- `args` is now persisted so the resume command reproduces the original invocation exactly; sessions persisted before this change fall back to a reconstructed `<url> [--tool]` command.

### Tests

- `tests/test-issue-1927-session-resume.mjs` — 31 unit assertions on the pure planning module (ordering, last-id selection, storm cap, solve-only).
- `tests/test-issue-1927-resume-notification.mjs` — 10 end-to-end assertions driving the real `monitorSessions`: the LAST session id reaches the notification; successful and `/hive` sessions stay unchanged.

All issue-1927 suites and the related monitor/store/docker/formatting suites pass locally. Documented under `docs/case-studies/issue-1927/README.md` ("which level resumes a killed `/solve`").

Addressed the review. Summary of this iteration:

**Conflicts** — resolved; PR is now `MERGEABLE` / `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`.

**Which level resumes (survival hierarchy).** Resume is offered by the level that *survives* the death of the one below it:

| Killed level | Surviving level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| AI tool (`claude`/`codex`/`gemini`) | `/solve` | `/solve` already auto-continues/`--resume`s the tool; many `Session ID:` markers result |
| `/solve` (e.g. OOM exit 137) | bot / `/hive` | the killed-session notification now **surfaces** a ready-to-run `solve <url> … --resume <lastSessionId>` command |
| bot / `/hive` | restart logic | durable session store resumes *tracking* and finally reports kills that happened while the bot was down |

**"Use the last of multiple sessions."** A single `/solve` run prints many `Session ID:` markers (auto-continue, watch restarts, manual chains). `readLastSessionIdFromLog`/`selectLastSessionId` pick the **last** marker from the log tail (most-advanced context), with a filesystem fallback (`findLatestSessionLogId`, newest `<uuid>.log`). End-to-end test writes a 2-session log and asserts the resume command names the **LAST**, never the first.

**Tool session id vs isolation id (self-caught bug, fixed in `1204a2c`).** `solve --resume` needs the **AI tool** session id (the `Session ID:` markers / `<uuid>.log` files), **not** `sessionInfo.sessionId` (the isolation id from `generateSessionId()` — wrong namespace). Removed the wrong-namespace fallback; if no real tool id is found, **no command is offered** (a bogus `--resume` id would be worse than none). New integration case asserts the isolation id never appears as a `--resume` argument.

**No crashes / backward compatibility.**
- The resume section is **additive** (existing `extraSections` path), emitted **only** for `killed` `/solve` sessions — successful sessions and `/hive` get nothing (asserted).
- The whole block is wrapped in try/catch so it can never break a notification.
- The bot **surfaces** the command rather than auto-relaunching (a job that reliably OOMs would storm); `planKilledSessionResume` caps any automatic resume (`maxAttempts: 1`).
- `args` added to persisted session fields so the resume reproduces the original invocation exactly.

**Verification.** Local full suite: **271/271 test files pass**. CI on the code commit `1204a2c`: `test-compilation`, `test-suites`, `test-execution`, `memory-check-linux`, `check-file-line-limits` all green. PR marked ready.
